# Bookmark.cards

> A self-hostable, open-source bookmark manager built with PHP and Kirby CMS. Users can save, tag, search, and export URLs. A free tier has a bookmark limit; a paid Premium tier removes it.

## What it does

- Stores bookmarks (URL + title + tags) per registered user
- Filters bookmarks by tag or searches by title, URL, or tag
- Detects duplicate URLs when adding a new bookmark
- Displays bookmarks as cards; if the title contains a known brand name, the card shows that brand's logo
- Exports bookmarks as JSON or CSV
- Works offline via a service worker (UpUp.js) that caches the bookmark list locally

## Tech stack

- **Backend**: PHP 8.2+, [Kirby CMS](https://getkirby.com/) 5 (flat-file, no database), dependencies via Composer
- **Payments**: Stripe via the local memberkit plugin (`site/plugins/memberkit`)
- **Frontend**: Vanilla JS, custom CSS (no framework, light/dark, WCAG AA), self-hosted Geist + Instrument Serif fonts, esbuild for build
- **Analytics**: Pirsch (privacy-friendly, no cookies)
- **Testing**: Pest (Stripe integration, brand logos, panel stats) and Cypress (end-to-end: auth, settings, bookmarks)
- **CI**: GitHub Actions (changelog), Dependabot (Composer, npm)

## Repository structure

- `site/` — Kirby CMS application (controllers, templates, snippets, blueprints, config, plugins: memberkit, brands, panel-stats)
- `content/` — Flat-file content (home page, user accounts)
- `assets/` — CSS and JS sources and builds, brand logos (`assets/brand-names`)
- `tests/` — Pest tests
- `cypress/` — End-to-end test specs
- `.github/` — Changelog workflow, Dependabot config

## Key design decisions

- Flat-file storage: content is stored as `.txt` files by Kirby; there is no relational database
- Brand logos are matched server-side by the `brands` plugin: the longest logo file name contained in the normalized title wins; no image processing at render time
- No social or collaborative features by design
- Free tier bookmark limit is configurable via `noPremiumLimit` in `site/config/config.php`
